两个不合理的点，让我不想玩下去了。 一是你boss曲线怎么设计的？不管我前面打的多顺，最顶配的一把6+2里有7个MAX核，甚至雪图boss前一个精英都秒杀，到了雪图boss瞬间巨刮无比，1只触手都要砍半天，以及远超之前boss的攻击频率攻击范围，你们程序员做他的时候多按了个0？ 二是局外养成也是奔着拉长玩家时间去的，玩了两三小时只解锁了最菜的一把武器。过一张图给1个石头，最贵的武器要三十多个是人？ 整的货币转化不知道怎么想的，直接摧毁了2种货币的存在意义。天赋不需要点吗？搞得好像天赋石很富裕一样。 战斗是挺爽的，但我打不过第四图啊，想玩新武器也玩不了。 我开一把止步第四图的，然后不要成长了天赋石全换成武器石，累死累活半小时大概也就十来个不会超过15.这和坐牢有啥区别？ 还有美工一坨，定价略高，如果没上面的问题这俩我都忍了。 你们该谢谢丝之歌，没这游戏提前打压了老菊的心态他肯定不会给你说这么多好话。
游戏好玩，但有的地方没给描述，我补充一个点希望帮到后面的玩家：局外成长解锁到8个虫核位，另外两个虫核位要在难度4以上解锁了装备合成之后，在局内收集金木冰火土五个元素碎片装备才能解锁，属于局内构筑。

The demo for this was extremely fun but the devs decided to make massive changes before the release which completely ruin the enjoyment levels. Before you could choose a main weapon and sub weapon at the start of your run, which allowed for some really fun builds. Now there is a core system with limited slots and matching same core types do different things. In addition to all of that, all of the bosses have massive amounts of health and are just huge sponges.

I cannot in good faith recomment this game. Not only are the Bosses are EXTREME DAMAGE SPONGES, but balance is non-existant. You start at difficulty 1 - which means you only have stage 1 unlocked. After you unlock difficulty 4 - and can progress deeper into the game, the issues become glaring and unfortunately, unavoidable. There is a huge difficulty spike in between difficulty 3 and 4. There are a lot of stats - crit damage, fixed damage, weapon damage, piecing damage, etc etc. On difficulty 4, you can try to focus on increasing any of those, but it does not make much difference. Feels like unless you have a VERY VERY specific build, boss battles will last FOREVER. The metaprogression itself is very light, without many truly relevant options, and does absolutely nothing to mitigate the problem. In several runs you'll be clearing stages easily, only to be stuck hitting the boss THOUSANDS of times. It completely destroys the flow of the game, not to mention it feels absolutely unfair and unbalanced. Game starts off well, you'll need to unlock a couple stages to notice the issue, but once it's there, it is there. A game that respects your time will provide you with different means to reach the end goal - different builds, that even if not fully min-maxed, can be fun, and effective. Not this game, at least for now. The devs are very present, so I wish them best of luck with this game and whatever next one they decide to develop.

优点：手感很好，特效华丽的强正反馈爽游。缺点：rogue方面不足。虫核将属性和武器专属词条合并让build可以随时更换是好事，但是虫核的属性过多了，不如删去几个虫核（比如很突兀的时间，嗜血），缩小虫核池，将这些删去的虫核效果做成小羁绊的联动，比如2-2，3-3，2-2-2，2-2-3，2-3-3等。特殊效果应该主要来自虫核的排列组合，而不是一定要凑成6或者4-4的大羁绊，让玩家开局就知道这局玩什么，怎么玩了，没有一点随机性。并且也正是因为虫核属性的强力羁绊必须高数量才能凑出，导致玩的时候花大量的时间重铸虫核，避免杂数羁绊，很影响节奏。

之前开终极装备的那个版本里 群里玩家提一些建议~意思终极装备可以刷新或者直接给挑选 不用总是SL刷自己想要的 SL的很麻烦~~结果那个群管理 猫娘 在那斩钉截铁的说 我们不会鼓励SL 设计人员绝对不会给终极装备刷新 这有违我们做游戏的初衷~我当时就说了 本来就是局外的东西 不在局内SL 这是两码事 而且这只是玩家建议 游戏毕竟是你们在做 作为玩家也仅仅是提提建议 至于改不改在于你们~（言下之意 你做不做是你的事 怼提建议的玩家算什么呢 你搁着原则nm呢？但当时还算保持客气 没真吵吵）~~ 但当时那个猫娘 回话就很不客气了 而且特别硬气：反正就是不会 你说再多也不会改（原话不止这一句 怼了很多句 大致就这个意思）~~ 好家伙 蹬鼻子上脸 但后面也没多论这事了 我这人还是很有原则的 既然你们公司这么定了 作为玩家确实不好再说什么 就当你是有原则 ~~ 隔了一段时间我现在上了下游戏 发现了个终极装备下面有个的刷新按钮~呵呵 虽然那个叫猫娘的群管理不知道和你们公司是什么关系 但既然他是你们定的管理员 那他说的话就默认代表你们公司对玩家的态度了~ 如果始终没变 我算你们坚持原则~那现在给了个刷新 那就别怪我不客气的说一句：婊子立牌坊 。 差评拿好不送~可以从这方面感知到这个公司对玩家真正的态度 ~属于是既想又要首鼠两端的典型了~装的很听取玩家意见 当玩家意见和自己设计方向有出入时又是另一幅嘴脸~但最后又因为提建议的人多而改变自己的立场 拥有灵活的身段~那你当初派个鸡头在群里怼玩家干什么？（吴京脸） 最后评价下游戏本身 横版动作肉鸽 我的游戏时长是挂机挂出来的实际游戏时间15~20多个小时的样子 算是有乐趣点 也有爽点 总体尚可~ 但是体量不大 内容也少~这个体量内容 和产品价格不匹配~和价格匹配的是美术方面~但制作组对玩家的态度 ~自行判断吧

为什么这么多评论说难。。。特地开了个新档打不到3小时速通难6，简单说下通用的机制 首先是进游戏后第一波，第一个虫核绝对绝对不要选武器专属词条，这是这游戏最大的坑，跟6虫核和双4虫核元素效果比起来武器词条是纯纯的垃圾，不是说不能通关，只是投入的资源跟产出完全不成比例。一开始随便用哪种元素（前期不推荐金元素，解锁完美通关送200金币的衣服之前很不好用）。除非钱花不完否则不要在商店花钱买虫核，这是所有获取渠道里性价比最低的一种 选好了这把要玩的虫核之后就没法换了，一定要只选同属性，不然会打的很难受。按c键能看到当前元素效果，解锁图鉴以后能看到所有4+4虫核组合效果，仔细看好触发条件跟强化的属性，这个游戏大后期build基本都是只强化一种攻击方式，不要想做六边形战士，火元素就强化攻速，雷元素就强化重攻击，除了武器伤害暴击这些比较万金油的之外，冲刺攻速重攻击冷却怒气等等都是根据build只强化一种 除了黄金斧的掠夺概率以外，升级绝对绝对绝对不要拿武器的特殊效果强化，尤其是各种轻攻击概率触发的效果，成型奇慢而且上限也不高，跟专属词条一个道理 最后是build的问题，这游戏基本所有build都可以在难6割草，无非是成型快慢和无脑程度的问题。整体来说我比较推荐几个打法： 高攻速武器+冰火，虫核词条拿火球强化跟冰冻增伤，血条消失术 任意武器+土木，词条拿藤蔓强化，极度无脑，afk通关 黄金斧+金币装+金虫核，词条选落金强化，非常安逸，后期钱花不完

这游戏是真的好，纯战斗爽肉鸽，关键上手难度极低，这才是游戏该有的样子。一直玩到肝出太刀才去看攻略，好久没有这么爽玩过了，我知道打金斧更好，但泳装太刀妹妹还能被动影分身这个设定太带感了。给制作团队几点建议： ​1，皮肤多出，而且就要擦边皮，要么甜妹要么烧鸡，别想着调性和政治正确，谁不让你擦边，谁就是希望贵司倒闭。 2，不同流派应该多点开花，强度都得够爽才行，现在玩下来只有近战输出爽。血牛，远程这两种玩起来爽感差挺多的，而且是不是未来还能开发一下上毒，反伤，真伤，一拳秒之类的流派？ 3，boss少来点大范围AOE技能，打怒再搞快一点，就是不走位就不躲技能，就是把大招当平A扔，都爽了那就爽到底，充分按摩大脑。就该像老一这种，boss一出来刚装完比就被一个三豆超必秒了谁不爱？你们别总觉得动作游戏就该拼操作拼走位，即时爽才是真的刚需，爽的成本太高那爽就没法长久。 ​4，必杀技和超必杀技都应该有动画才对，而且动画要特写一些绅士部位，人物动作奔放一点。现在这个动作看起来太呆了，给个按E跳过设定，也不担心打乱战斗节奏。 ​5，条件允许，最好是有配音，起码比杀和超必要有名字，出大招的那一刻就是要告诉全世界爷这招有多帅有多猛，一拳送boss全家上天，这种玩家心理才是喜欢动作爽游的玩家心里。”究极无敌宇宙灭亡拳“跟”随便打一拳“，这两者显然不是一码事。

This game has the most basic combat mechanics I've seen in a while. Hold down Square, spam X to dodge. Press LB sometimes and RT when gauge fills up. There you go, that's the entire game. The fighting is smooth, I can't really tell if the "Instect cores" actually make that much of a difference from one to another. Some boss fights just require to keep dashing constantly with next to no pattern learning required. The art is good as well and it's well optimised. That being said, I honestly can't recommend this, it's just not that fun to me and there are a lot of better options available in the Roguelike/lite genre. 6/10

I bought this game because I saw the devs were active with answering reviews here on steam. That's pretty rare so I thought it was a good sign and the game looked kind of interesting from the youtube vids I saw on it. But holy F is it a terrible game. The weapons feel like dog-poop. The numbers start out way too high so they make no sense. Why am I hitting for 800 trillion billion after 1 hour of gameplay? The super skills are way too overpowered. I literally oneshot a boss with it. Everything just feels floaty and meaningless, the impact of the weapons are non-existent, the autoaim on the first ranged weapon SUCKS. You can tell how janky and badly coded it is right away. The lightning gauntlet also sucks. The heavy attack and rage attack on it barely does any damage, only the R2/LT ability is good. The attack speed is way too high. You should start off with a MUCH slower attack speed so that whenever you get high attack speed it feels meaningful. This game is also way too fast-paced and has way too high numbers for there not to be a DPS meter or damage breakdown. The UI in the game sucks complete ass. Almost nothing is explained (well) or properly. Why are the relics that you equip part of the same backpack as the passive bonuses? It looks and feels bad. It makes me even unsure if the passives are 'equipped' or active. Why do they clutter the same slots? Needlessly confusing. Absolute crap game. There are much better games out there. And at this price point this is a robbery. I also hate how there are a max of 8 relic slots, which makes getting upgrades feel pointless really quick. Imagine if Slay the Spire had a max cap of 8 relics. How boring would that be? About as boring as this game actually. Also, the mobs sometimes get stunned when you hit them? Sometimes they don't? I have no clue what indicator to look for whether or not a mob is able to be stunlocked or not, and often times they don't really have any warning that they are about to attack so I get hit unfairly. Trash indicators and telegraphs. The game boils down to holding down the autoattack button and pressing rage/heavy attack on cooldown while you dash around, with crap-feeling weapons with no impact and you can barely even make sense of the damage numbers because of how big the numbers are and how bad the visibility of the numbers are. I don't like female-only games either. Make a badass male character with some 'oomph'-factor in the weapon animations. There is no story here either and the design on this female character is also pretty trash so you might as well make a male character to appeal to a much wider audience. This is a cheaply made mobile garbage cashgrab game. It has no business costing 19 dollars. Shape of Dreams is an INFINITELY better game for the same price

This game is crazy hard, makes me hate it at times, but the next run or the one after goes better. When you're in the zone it's awesome, when you're in danger zone you wish you could retry the boss. The main character is really cool, her skins can make her sexier, but i prefer the cooler ones, they fit more with the apocalyptic aesthetic the game puts you in. [h1]COOL POTENTIAL, LACKING THE X FACTOR [/h1] [h3]Pros [/h3] The gameplay is pretty smooth, and i actually like that each weapon is different enough to feel distinct, and also have special affixes that can make them operate differently, rather than just numbers go up. Movement and reaction also feel very responsive. There is also a toggle to adjust the screen effects if you find it too cluttered, that was a nice touch. Enemies are varied enough and poses decent challenge, the bosses also have a pretty wide set of moves. It's also nice that skins provide special effects rather than just pure cosmetics. [h3]Cons [/h3] The game feels... unfinished? Incomplete or unpolished? It lacks that X factor that makes it special. From the beginning, you just immediately start the game and get thristed into the stage, no story, nothing. Stories are all purely lore drops from enemies, and you piece them yourself on the archive. I really feel that it isn't that hard to add some story and context to make the entire adventure more coherent. The balance is kinda whack. There is a total 6 difficulty levels, and you go up in difficulty as you progress through the stages. The thing is, somewhere in difficulty 4, this point is somewhat the hardest, since you will encounter the 4th boss, and it can be very very tanky if your build is not done well. See, the thing is, you don't just pick items like normal roguelikes, here you have to stack them properly. And if you build them properly, you can get so overpowered and do something akin to 1 hit ko, if not, you are battling the boss for an entire 5 mins or more.... And in the last few stages, it's all a dps match, either you kill fast, or the battle get so long and you die. But in difficulty 5 & 6, you get more affixes that difficulty 5 & 6 are actually easier than 3 & 4. Plus, after you finish the final stages, there's really nothing much to it other than trying to run them again with different weapons. There are no changes to the stages nor bosses, so the game feels rather short. [h3]Summary [/h3] A decent game with a few cool moments here and there, but still falling short of that X factor that makes it a special roguelike. Worth it on sale.

Star Fire: Eternal Cycle is an action roguelite developed by Ethereal Fish Studio and published by Indie Herb Games that combines side-scrolling combat, progression-driven replayability, and build experimentation into a fast-paced arcade experience. Rather than relying on heavy storytelling or lengthy setup sequences, the game focuses on movement, combat flow, and repeatable progression systems designed to encourage players to constantly improve through repeated attempts. The result is a game built around momentum, adaptability, and mechanical growth. The structure follows familiar roguelite principles while adding enough flexibility to make progression feel rewarding across multiple sessions. Players enter dangerous encounters, battle through increasingly difficult enemy groups, gather upgrades, and attempt to survive long enough to create stronger builds capable of overcoming tougher opposition. Failure remains part of the experience rather than punishment. Even unsuccessful attempts contribute resources and unlock opportunities that strengthen future runs, creating a gameplay loop designed around steady improvement. Combat immediately becomes the strongest feature. Controls emphasize responsiveness and movement precision while encouraging players to stay active during encounters. Standing still rarely becomes a safe option. Success depends heavily on positioning, timing, and understanding enemy behavior while balancing offensive pressure with survival instincts. The pacing remains consistently energetic, helping maintain engagement even during repeated sessions. One of the game's more impressive strengths comes through build customization. Combat approaches can change dramatically depending on weapon selection, upgrades, and elemental combinations discovered during progression. Different combinations create opportunities to experiment with varying playstyles rather than forcing players into rigid combat roles. Some builds prioritize aggressive damage output while others reward defensive stability or specialized synergies. That flexibility creates one of the game's strongest long-term advantages. Elemental systems contribute heavily to replay value as well. Multiple elemental options introduce meaningful choices throughout progression, encouraging experimentation across repeated runs. Strong combinations can create highly satisfying combat moments where mechanics begin working together smoothly, rewarding players who invest time learning how different systems interact. The progression systems outside individual runs also help strengthen long-term motivation. Unlockable content, permanent upgrades, and additional customization options create consistent incentives to continue playing beyond immediate completion goals. Growth feels steady without becoming overly dependent on grinding. Progression systems support improvement rather than replacing player skill entirely. Movement mechanics deserve recognition because they help define combat pacing significantly. Dodging enemy attacks and maintaining proper positioning remain essential throughout the experience. Encounters reward players who understand spacing and movement timing rather than relying entirely on raw statistics. Mechanical improvement consistently matters alongside progression systems. The game also benefits from smaller design choices that keep repeated attempts feeling less predictable. Hidden areas, unexpected discoveries, and shifting opportunities during progression help preserve excitement during longer play periods. Even familiar content maintains freshness through changing build possibilities and varied progression outcomes. Visually, Star Fire: Eternal Cycle adopts a colorful arcade-inspired presentation that complements the gameplay effectively. Combat remains readable despite increasingly chaotic encounters, which becomes especially important during later stages where enemy density and build complexity increase significantly. Visual effects support combat impact without overwhelming clarity. Enemy encounters scale steadily throughout progression, creating a challenge curve that encourages stronger decision-making over time. Later encounters demand better understanding of mechanics and stronger adaptation skills. Progression feels rewarding because stronger execution naturally creates stronger results. The game naturally carries limitations associated with progression-focused roguelites. Certain runs may feel significantly stronger depending on available upgrades and build combinations, creating occasional balance inconsistencies. Players looking primarily for narrative-driven experiences may also find the lighter storytelling emphasis less engaging than combat-focused systems. However, Star Fire: Eternal Cycle clearly prioritizes gameplay systems first and succeeds because of that focus. The game avoids unnecessary complexity and instead concentrates heavily on making combat satisfying and progression rewarding. Every mechanic exists primarily to support replayability and experimentation. What makes the experience memorable is how effectively it balances familiarity with flexibility. Core systems remain accessible while offering enough variation to encourage long-term investment. Strong movement design, satisfying combat flow, and meaningful build experimentation create an experience that consistently rewards persistence. Star Fire: Eternal Cycle succeeds because it understands what makes action roguelites enjoyable. Improvement feels earned. Repetition creates mastery rather than monotony. Progression supports player growth without replacing it. Star Fire: Eternal Cycle delivers satisfying action combat, rewarding progression systems, and excellent replay value while successfully blending arcade pacing with modern roguelite design principles. Rating: 8/10
